reply: Sorry about the dropouts with your Lumen bulb pack. Band steering on mesh routers can confuse them, so please try these steps: (1) In the router app, create a dedicated 2.4 GHz network or temporarily disable band steering. (2) Hold the device's reset button for 10 seconds until the light blinks amber. (3) Set the device up again in the app on the 2.4 GHz network. If it still drops within 24 hours of following these steps, reply with your router model and we will escalate the issue to our side.

Thanks for reporting this, and sorry about the dropouts. We know of a band steering mesh router that can push a device onto the wrong band, so your 2.4 GHz band is likely the culprit. Please reply with the last four digits of the card or the order number of the Nook speaker and we will take a look. If the device is still dropping after 24 hours, please reply with the email address and the current network password and we will re-link the device on our side.

Thanks for reporting this, and apologies for the dropouts. We know about a band-steering issue with some mesh routers, so if you have one, please pull down on the device list in the app and toggle band steering off for 24 hours. That forces the router to switch bands itself, and most band steering apps show this as a pending update. Once it is released, a new app version will roll out first. Until: reply with the email on your account and we will re-link the device from our side.

Sorry about the trouble with your Lumen bulb pack. I looked at the device list and found a device on the 2.4 GHz band that is connecting to your network. Please reply with the 2.4 GHz network name and the router model so we can remove the device from the 2.4 GHz band. Once we have those, you can try resetting the Lumen bulb pack or holding the device's reset button for 10 seconds until the light blinks amber. If it reconnects within 24 hours, reply with the email on the account and we will remove the 2.4 GHz band from our system.

Sorry about the trouble with your Breeze air purifier. Each mesh router has its own private 2.4 GHz band, so connecting two devices on that band will keep both running independently. Here is what usually happens: the router bands switch between 2.4 GHz and 2.4 GHz band steering, and some devices try to join on the 2.4 GHz band first. When the 2.4 GHz band switches, those devices drop out until the 2.4 GHz band reverts. To fix this, turn band steering off for 24 hours, then enable it again. If the Breeze air purifier still drops after 24 hours, reply with the last four digits of the card and the order of the devices on the router, and we will take a look.

Sorry about the trouble with your Lumen bulb pack. Band steering on mesh routers can pull devices onto the wrong band, causing this. (2) Hold the device's reset button for 10 seconds until the light blinks amber. (3) Set the device up again in the app on the 2.4 GHz network. If it still drops after 24 hours, reply with your router model and we will escalate the issue to our side.

Sorry about the trouble with your Nook speaker. I looked at the device in our network monitoring tool and see it connecting on both 2.4 GHz and 2.5 GHz bands. If it drops again after 24 hours, let us know and we will escalate the issue to our network team.
